legal.headline: Is the Collegium system failing women?
legal.hook: Is the Collegium system failing women?
legal.summary: Seven decades after the establishment of the Supreme Court, having only 3 women among 37 judges is not a statistic that an institution committed to constitutional equality should overlook.
legal.contextNote: Bar & Bench focuses on gender representation within the apex court, pointing out that seven decades post-establishment, the Supreme Court has only 3 women among 37 judges. Judicial appointments governed by Articles 124(2) and 217 of the Constitution of India—and operationalized by the Collegium system established under the Second Judges Case (Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India, 1993)—lack explicit affirmative action mandates for gender diversity. (1) In-house counsel managing corporate ESG frameworks should prepare for intensified judicial scrutiny on corporate gender compliance, particularly mandatory woman director appointments under Section 149(1) of the Companies Act, 2013 and strict POSH Act compliance. (2) Legal teams handling cross-border M&A must ensure robust workplace diversity disclosures to satisfy foreign institutional investors sensitive to institutional gender parity deficits in key jurisdiction leadership.
